report: The 10-year-old boy's bilateral congenital cataracts, long narrow face, mandibular prognathism, and characteristic dental findings—screwdriver-shaped incisors, Talon's cusps, supernumerary cusps, generalized spacing—point to Nance-Horan syndrome. Dental radiographs showing supernumerary teeth, pulp stones, and taurodontism further corroborate this phenotype. These systemic and dental features are not explained by ectodermal dysplasia or isolated dental anomaly, both refuted by cataracts and facial dysmorphism. With radiologist and laboratory physician concurrence, Nance-Horan syndrome is the most likely diagnosis.
